title: Completeness of a normalized limit after open extension
statement: For a prime l, finite coefficient field E, Operations o and a quasi-compact open immersion j:U->V, if N is Good on U and shriek(j)(N) is Good on V, then ringedOpen(j)(coefficientSequenceLimit(N)) is intrinsically complete.

proof.text: Apply purNormalizedReconstructionOfScheme to the specified source calculus and the normalization component hN.1 of Good. Its first clause proves completeness of the actual coefficientSequenceLimit(N); no invertibility of l on U is needed.

Use the proved dvrOpenModel_exists helper of OpenQuotientKoszulCompleteness to obtain a projection-normalized OpenDvrOpenModel O. The proved dvrOpen_complete helper of OpenDvrIntrinsicOpenTransport carries source completeness through O.jShriek using exactness, countable products and the actual uniformizer scalar. These helpers impose no characteristic hypothesis, unlike the older assembly theorem.

Apply openDvr_ringed_identification to O to identify its derived extension naturally with the specified ringedOpen. Choose a prime p different from l. The complete_iff_local helper converts quotient completeness to local principal completeness, integralLocallyComplete_iso transports that condition through the component of the natural isomorphism, and complete_iff_local converts back. The auxiliary prime exists independently of the schemes. The output Good hypothesis and the operations parameter are retained in the signature but are not needed by this argument.

proof_origin.place: Integral open-factor completeness: reuse proved DVR model construction, principal-completion preservation, and ringed identification; no new statements.

lean.statement: theorem integralOpenLimitComplete (o : Operations l E) {U V : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ V) [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] (N : System l E U) (hN : Good l E U N) (hJ : Good l E V ((Operations.shriek l E o j).obj N)) : IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E V none ((ringedOpen l E j).obj ((coefficientSequenceLimit l E U).obj N))
